questions.cardText:
[History] What event is considered the symbolic start of the French Revolution?
A. The signing of the Treaty of Versailles
B. The Storming of the Bastille
C. The execution of Louis XVI
Answer: B. The storming of the Bastille on July 14, 1789, is commemorated annually as the national holiday in France celebrating liberty and the birth of the French Republic. Although only seven prisoners were found inside the Bastille and it was already scheduled for demolition, the event symbolized the end of the king’s absolute power and the rise of the people’s voice in government.
questions.de: Welches Ereignis vom 14. Juli 1789, an das der französische Nationalfeiertag erinnert, gilt als symbolischer Beginn der Französischen Revolution?
questions.en: What event of 14 July 1789, commemorated by France's national holiday, is considered the symbolic start of the French Revolution?

timeline.labelEn: Parisian revolutionaries storm the Bastille, the flashpoint of the French Revolution
timeline.labelDe: Pariser Revolutionäre stürmen die Bastille – der Auslöser der Französischen Revolution

questions.notes: Card correct: Wikipedia calls the fall of the Bastille the flashpoint of the French Revolution; it held only seven prisoners and was already scheduled for demolition. The Fête nationale commemorates both 14 July 1789 and the Fête de la Fédération of 1790.

questions.cardText:
[Physics] What property of a sound wave determines its pitch?
A. Amplitude
B. Waveform
C. Frequency
Answer: C.
questions.de: Welche physikalische Eigenschaft einer Schallwelle bestimmt die Tonhöhe, die wir hören?
questions.en: What physical property of a sound wave determines the pitch we hear?

timeline.labelEn: Marin Mersenne's Harmonie universelle gives the earliest formulation of the laws for a vibrating string's frequency
timeline.labelDe: Marin Mersennes „Harmonie universelle“ formuliert erstmals die Gesetze für die Frequenz einer schwingenden Saite

questions.notes: Card correct: pitch is a perceptual property that orders sounds on a frequency-related scale and is quantified as a frequency (Wikipedia: Pitch (music)). Timeline from Wikipedia: Marin Mersenne (Harmonie universelle, 1636; Mersenne's laws).
